name: Port Vesper
basis: Original setting written for Prospero Companion: an orbital trading station that flies beside the Long Meridian, the built-in generation ship. Nothing is taken from any published setting.
summary: A station of about seven thousand people that left Earth after the Meridian, caught up with it thirty-seven years ago and now flies alongside: a trading port, a shipyard, coffee terraces, a sheep deck and a great window onto the ship three hours away by shuttle.

curated-2026-10.title: Port Vesper, written for Prospero Companion
curated-2026-10.note: An invented station. Its rings, trades, prices and calendar are written for it; every business, family and person named is fictional. Prices and rents are in credits, monthly. Coordinates sit far out in the Pacific for distance estimates only.

neighborhoods.name: The Concourse
neighborhoods.summary: The docking hub at the centre of the station: shuttle gates, customs, hotels for traders and the departures board everyone checks twice.

neighborhoods.name: Market Ring
neighborhoods.summary: The station's shopping and eating ring: coffee houses, tailors, spice stalls, restaurants and the noise of a place that trades for a living.

neighborhoods.name: Spinward Terraces
neighborhoods.summary: Terraced homes with wide windows on the spinward side, where the yard owners, captains and old Earth families live.

neighborhoods.name: The Yards
neighborhoods.summary: The shipyard and foundry, building shuttles, drones and spare rings for the Meridian, with welders' bunks and a canteen that never closes.

neighborhoods.name: Garden Ring
neighborhoods.summary: The station's farm ring: a coffee plantation under lamps, a sheep deck for the wool everyone on the Meridian wants and a green park in the middle.

neighborhoods.name: Low Ring
neighborhoods.summary: The cheapest ring, half a gravity and full of young crews, music bars, late kitchens and cabins three to a room.

neighborhoods.name: Observation Spoke
neighborhoods.summary: A long spoke reaching out to the station's great window, with the school, a gallery and the best view of the Meridian turning in the dark.

neighborhoods.name: Old Hull
neighborhoods.summary: The original Earth-built core of the station, all scuffed panels and stencilled deck numbers, with the arrival museum, the chapel and the oldest bar aboard.

places.name: The Departures Hall
places.summary: A bright hall under the great board, where shuttles to the Meridian leave on the hour and families wave from the rail.

places.name: The Gatehouse
places.summary: A traders' hotel by the gates with real beds, a quiet bar and breakfast served until the last shuttle.

places.name: Gate Six Coffee
places.summary: The station's most famous coffee bar, roasting beans from the Garden Ring and selling them by the tin to Meridian visitors.

places.name: Customs Canteen
places.summary: A plain canteen behind the customs desks, with the cheapest hot lunch on the station and the best gossip.

places.name: The Last Shuttle
places.summary: A bar named for everyone who has missed it, with a clock showing the next launch and a crowd that does not care.

places.name: The Spice Arcade
places.summary: A covered arcade of spice merchants, pickles and dried fruit, smelling of cardamom from one end to the other.

places.name: Wool & Weft
places.summary: A knitwear shop selling real station wool, the most wanted present on the Meridian.

places.name: The Copper Pan
places.summary: A bustling bistro with a menu that changes with each supply run: braised greens, fresh pasta and real cheese.

places.name: Ring Bakehouse
places.summary: A bakery that fills the ring with the smell of rye and cinnamon at the morning bell.

places.name: The Little Ring Theatre
places.summary: A hundred-seat theatre over the shops, with comedy, cabaret and touring players from the Meridian.

places.name: Noodle Lane
places.summary: Six noodle counters in a row, each claiming to be the original.

places.name: The Terrace Wine Bar
places.summary: A wine bar pouring the station's own vintages from the Garden Ring vines, with a window wall onto the stars.

places.name: The Spinward Promenade
places.summary: A planted promenade along the terraces, where nannies push prams and captains walk their dogs.

places.name: The Captains' Table
places.summary: A formal dining room where yard owners close deals over station lamb and too much wine.

places.name: Terrace Salon
places.summary: A hairdresser and beauty salon where the Terraces get their news before the feed does.

places.name: The Tea Room
places.summary: A genteel tea room with tiered cakes and a pianist on rest-day afternoons.

places.name: Foundry Canteen
places.summary: A twenty-four-hour canteen for welders and fitters: pies, fried rice and tea strong enough to weld with.

places.name: The Slipway Gallery
places.summary: A viewing gallery over the slipway where a new shuttle is always half built.

places.name: The Rivet
places.summary: A loud yard bar with arm-wrestling on Fridays and a ceiling covered in signed welding masks.

places.name: Yard Gym
places.summary: A no-frills gym with heavy weights and a boxing ring the yard crews fight charity bouts in.

places.name: The Makers' Bench
places.summary: A public workshop with offcuts from the yard, where anyone can learn to weld on rest days.

places.name: The Coffee Terraces
places.summary: Stepped rows of coffee bushes under warm lamps, with tours, tastings and pickers in wide hats.

places.name: The Sheep Deck
places.summary: A grassy deck of sheep kept for their wool, with shearing days that draw a crowd from the Meridian.

places.name: Green Commons
places.summary: The station's central lawn, with picnic tables, a bandstand and the only grass you can lie on for three hours' flight.

places.name: The Vineyard House
places.summary: A farm restaurant among the vines with long lunches of lamb, bread and the house red.

places.name: The Potting Shed
places.summary: A cafe in a former potting shed, serving lamp-grown coffee and scones to farm hands.

places.name: Night Kitchen
places.summary: A late kitchen of skewers, flatbreads and hot sauce, busiest after the bars close.

places.name: Half-G
places.summary: A club in half gravity where the dancing is mostly jumping, and the jumps are very high.

places.name: The Bunkhouse
places.summary: A crowded bar of young crews, open-mic nights and cheap shots named after shuttle routes.

places.name: Spin Cycle
places.summary: A laundrette and cafe where half the ring meets on a rest-day morning.

places.name: Groove Bay
places.summary: A record shop of Earth music, station bands and the odd Meridian folk recording.

places.name: The Great Window
places.summary: A window forty metres wide at the end of the spoke, with the Meridian turning slowly in the dark beyond it.

places.name: Spoke Library
places.summary: The station library, shared with the school, with a corner of real paper books shipped from Earth.

places.name: The Window Cafe
places.summary: A cafe right under the Great Window, where the coffee is ordinary and the view is not.

places.name: Spoke Gallery
places.summary: A small art gallery of station painters and photographs of the Meridian across thirty-seven years alongside.

places.name: The Spoke Pool
places.summary: A long swimming pool lit from below, with lane swimming at dawn and family swims after school.

places.name: Museum of the Arrival
places.summary: The story of the station's chase across the dark and the day it caught up with the Meridian, with the first handshake on film.

places.name: The Hull Chapel
places.summary: A small chapel in a storage bay, with candles in jars and a wall of photos from Earth.

places.name: The First Pour
places.summary: The oldest bar on the station, where the founding crew drank the first beer brewed aboard and the tap still says so.

places.name: Stencil Diner
places.summary: A diner under stencilled deck numbers, serving pancakes and coffee from the first shift to the last.

places.name: Old Hull Market
places.summary: A rest-day market of secondhand tools, heirlooms from Earth and old station uniforms.

employers.name: Vesper Port Authority
employers.summary: Runs the gates, the shuttle schedule to the Meridian and customs.

employers.name: Vesper Yards
employers.summary: Builds shuttles, drones and spare ring sections for the station and the Meridian.

employers.name: Vesper Trading House
employers.summary: The station's biggest trading firm, buying and selling with the Meridian.

employers.name: Garden Ring Estates
employers.summary: Grows the station's coffee and vines and keeps the sheep.

employers.name: Station Operations
employers.summary: Keeps the air, water, power and spin running.

employers.name: Market Ring Hospitality
employers.summary: The station's hotels, restaurants and coffee bars.

employers.name: Vesper Feed
employers.summary: The station's news and music broadcast, with a weekly show for the Meridian.

employers.name: Vesper Watch
employers.summary: The station's security and rescue crews.

employers.name: Station Council
employers.summary: The station's council and the offices that talk to the Meridian's Voyage Council.

employers.name: Low Ring Venues
employers.summary: The clubs, bars and stages of the Low Ring.

career_hubs.name: The port
career_hubs.summary: Gates, customs, traders and the shops and hotels that live off them.

career_hubs.name: The yards
career_hubs.summary: The shipyard, the foundry and station operations.

transit.name: On foot
transit.summary: Each ring walks round in twenty minutes; the spokes are long, and most people take the lifts.

transit.name: Ring shuttle
transit.summary: Little carts that run round each ring and across to the Concourse every few minutes.

transit.name: Spoke lifts
transit.summary: Lifts up and down the spokes, from full gravity on the rings to none at the Concourse.

climate.summary: Climate-controlled rings: mild all year, warm on the Garden Ring, cool in the Yards.

annual_events.name: Shearing Days
annual_events.summary: The flock is sheared on the Sheep Deck, with a fair, a knitting race and visitors from the Meridian.

annual_events.name: Arrival Week
annual_events.summary: A week of parties for the day the station caught up with the Meridian, ending with a shuttle parade.

annual_events.name: Shuttle Launch
annual_events.summary: A new shuttle rolls off the slipway and is christened with a bottle of the house red.

annual_events.name: Coffee Harvest
annual_events.summary: The coffee terraces are picked and the whole station smells of roasting for a week.

annual_events.name: Window Nights
annual_events.summary: The spoke goes dark so everyone can watch the Meridian's lights turning past the Great Window.

annual_events.name: Low Ring Music Week
annual_events.summary: Bands from both ships play every bar on the ring, and nobody sleeps.

careers.name: Shepherd
careers.summary: Keeps the Sheep Deck's flock fed, sheared and out of the coffee bushes.

careers.name: Coffee roaster
careers.summary: Roasts the Garden Ring's beans for the station and the tins that go over to the Meridian.

careers.name: Gate announcer
careers.summary: Calls every shuttle departure and arrival on the Concourse, and every name of every passenger who is late.

local_color.name: Station red
local_color.summary: The house red from the Garden Ring vines, rough when young and much better than anyone on the Meridian admits.

local_color.name: Gate Six blend
local_color.summary: The station's own roast, sold by the tin to every visitor from the Meridian.

local_color.name: Station lamb
local_color.summary: Lamb from the Sheep Deck, rare and dear, roasted for Midwinter and big deals.

local_color.name: Cardamom buns
local_color.summary: Sticky cardamom buns from the Ring Bakehouse, carried back to the Meridian by the boxful.

local_color.name: Yard pie
local_color.summary: A pie the size of a welding mask, filled with whatever the canteen had left.

local_color.name: "Mind the gate"
local_color.summary: Goodbye on Port Vesper, said to anyone heading for a shuttle.

local_color.name: "We caught up, didn't we?"
local_color.summary: Said when something hard finally works out, after the station's long chase.

local_color.name: Meridian cousins
local_color.summary: Station families keep up with a family on the Meridian, swapping wool for honey cake and visiting on Arrival Day.

local_color.name: Proposals at the Great Window
local_color.summary: Proposing at the Great Window with the Meridian passing behind is the station's favourite romantic cliche.

local_color.name: Signed masks
local_color.summary: Every welder signs their first mask and hangs it on the ceiling of the Rivet.

local_color.name: Vesper Rovers
local_color.summary: The station's hoopball team, who travel to the Meridian for away games and lose most of them.

local_color.name: The fifteenth crew member
local_color.summary: The founding crew was fourteen, but every photo of them shows fifteen, and nobody can say who the last one is.

local_color.name: The other station
local_color.summary: Some say a second station left Earth after Vesper and is still chasing the Meridian. The Port Authority says nothing.

local_color.name: Earth time
local_color.summary: The station still counts years by the Earth calendar, which makes every meeting with the Meridian's voyage years a small argument.

local_color.name: The hourly shuttle
local_color.summary: Shuttles leave for the Meridian on the hour from the Departures Hall; the flight takes about three hours.

prices.per: for one, with a glass of station red
a day's take-home for an ordinary job

holidays.name: Arrival Day
holidays.summary: The day Port Vesper caught up with the Meridian after a fourteen-year chase, with a toast at the Departures Hall.

holidays.name: Station New Year
holidays.summary: New year by the Earth calendar the station still keeps, with a countdown on the great board.

holidays.name: Earth Remembrance
holidays.summary: People share photos and stories of Earth at the Hull Chapel and the Window Cafe.

holidays.name: Yards Day
holidays.summary: A day off for the yard crews, with a parade of drones down the Concourse.

holidays.name: Midwinter
holidays.summary: Candles in every window, mulled wine from the Garden Ring and presents swapped with Meridian friends.

quirks.text: checks the departures board even when not travelling
quirks.bio: I check the board. I am not going anywhere. I just like to know.

quirks.text: keeps a photo of Earth by the bed
quirks.bio: There is a photo of Earth by my bed. My grandmother took it.
Meridian folk are all cousins to me.

quirks.text: can tell a coffee bean's terrace by the smell
quirks.bio: Give me a bean and I will tell you which terrace it grew on.

quirks.text: has a signed welding mask on the Rivet's ceiling
quirks.bio: My mask is on the Rivet ceiling, third row from the bar.

quirks.text: watches the Meridian turn past the Great Window every evening
quirks.bio: Every evening, the Great Window. It is cheaper than the cinema.

quirks.text: argues about Earth years and voyage years
quirks.bio: It is the Earth year that counts. Fight me.
